transcription.text: A gas screen. No alarm showing. Calm or a detector gone quiet? A good screen says which.
Start with the top line. Check. The newest readings age and four of five detectors reporting.
The gas dashboard opens on overview. Five detectors, four online. Live alarms counts
alerts nobody has acknowledged. Acknowledged, though someone has not yet closed.
Three gases. Limits on each card. H2S alarms above 10 parts per million.
Combustible gas alarms above 20% LEL. Oxygen has a low limit, 19.5. The page says its alarm
is not raised yet. Cards show the worst of four reporting. The page names the fifth as offline.
Readiness reads not ready, and a list says what needs attention.
Wallboard and phone.
Phone views open by web address, not from the menu. The answer is big. Check. Not confirmed
safe. One detector not reporting. The phone view carries the same words, and the same list of what
needs attention. This page lists each detector. The fifth reads check. Last known values, not
current. Show detail opens its readings. The newest three read closed. No button. On an
acknowledged row with edit access, this is where you close it.
Open alerts counts everything not yet closed. Twelve. All acknowledged. So live alarms on the
overview read zero. Closing is recorded here. It is not sent to Blackline. An alert closed here
stays open in Blackline Live. Blackline is the gas vendor. The page also names what is missing.
No alert timeline. No assignee. No closed count. Compliance lists the limits. Exposure and exceedances
say not available yet. Not an empty chart that reads is all clear. Detectors report to the vendor's
cloud. A black box to us. WakeCap asks that cloud for readings on a timer. Each detector reports on
its own schedule, so each reading shows its age. An offline detector reads check, like the fifth.
A quiet screen is not an answer, so gas shows its gaps. If your project has it, open it and read the
top line.
